rivers.name: Ganga
rivers.source: Bhagirathi and Alaknanda meet at Devprayag
rivers.mouth: Bay of Bengal, through its delta system
rivers.route: Uttarakhand → Uttar Pradesh → Bihar → Jharkhand → West Bengal
rivers.note: The Yamuna and Son join from the right; Ghaghara and Gandak join from the left.

rivers.name: Yamuna
rivers.note: A right-bank tributary of the Ganga. The Chambal is a tributary of the Yamuna.

rivers.name: Chambal
rivers.note: Part of the Ganga drainage system through the Yamuna; associated with ravine landscapes.

rivers.name: Gandak
rivers.route: Nepal → Bihar, along part of the Uttar Pradesh boundary
rivers.note: A left-bank Himalayan tributary of the Ganga.

rivers.name: Ghaghara
rivers.source: Tibetan Himalaya; known as Karnali in Nepal
rivers.route: Tibet → Nepal → Uttar Pradesh and Bihar
rivers.note: The Karnali–Ghaghara is an important Himalayan river system feeding the Ganga.

rivers.name: Son
rivers.note: A right-bank tributary of the Ganga, rising in the Peninsular plateau.

rivers.name: Indus
rivers.source: Tibetan plateau, near the Manasarovar region
rivers.note: The Punjab tributaries ultimately join the Indus; its main course drains to the Arabian Sea.

rivers.name: Jhelum
rivers.note: Flows through the Kashmir Valley and Wular Lake before joining the Chenab.

rivers.name: Chenab
rivers.source: Chandra and Bhaga meet at Tandi
rivers.mouth: Indus system, through Punjab river confluences
rivers.note: The Chandra and Bhaga join to form the Chenab.

rivers.name: Ravi
rivers.route: Himachal Pradesh → Punjab border region → Pakistan
rivers.note: One of the five rivers associated with Punjab and part of the Indus system.

rivers.name: Beas
rivers.note: The Beas joins the Sutlej at Harike in Punjab.

rivers.name: Sutlej
rivers.note: Enters India near Shipki La and receives the Beas at Harike.

rivers.name: Brahmaputra
rivers.mouth: Bay of Bengal, through the Ganga–Meghna delta system
rivers.note: Known as Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet, Siang/Dihang in Arunachal Pradesh, and Jamuna in Bangladesh.

rivers.name: Teesta
rivers.note: A Himalayan tributary of the Brahmaputra system, not the Ganga system.

rivers.name: Godavari
rivers.note: The largest Peninsular river system; also called Dakshin Ganga.

rivers.name: Krishna
rivers.note: The Bhima and Tungabhadra are major tributaries of the Krishna.

rivers.name: Tungabhadra
rivers.source: Tunga and Bhadra meet at Koodli, Karnataka
rivers.note: Formed by the Tunga and Bhadra; it is a tributary of the Krishna.

rivers.name: Mahanadi
rivers.note: Hirakud Dam is built across the Mahanadi in Odisha.

rivers.name: Kaveri
rivers.note: An east-flowing river with its source in the Western Ghats; also written Cauvery.

rivers.name: Narmada
rivers.route: Madhya Pradesh → Maharashtra/Gujarat boundary region → Gujarat
rivers.note: Flows west through a rift valley between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges.

rivers.name: Tapi
rivers.note: Also called Tapti. Like the Narmada, it flows west towards the Arabian Sea.

rivers.name: Kosi
rivers.note: A Himalayan tributary joining the Ganga in Bihar.

rivers.name: Gomti
rivers.note: A Ganga tributary flowing through Lucknow.

rivers.name: Ramganga
rivers.note: A Himalayan tributary joining the Ganga in Uttar Pradesh.

rivers.name: Betwa
rivers.note: A peninsular tributary of the Yamuna within the Ganga system.

rivers.name: Ken
rivers.note: A Bundelkhand river joining the Yamuna.

rivers.name: Subansiri
rivers.note: A northern Himalayan tributary of the Brahmaputra.

rivers.name: Dibang
rivers.note: Joins the Siang–Lohit river network in the upper Assam region.

rivers.name: Lohit
rivers.note: Joins the Siang–Dibang network before the main Brahmaputra course in Assam.

rivers.name: Manas
rivers.note: A northern tributary flowing from Bhutan to the Brahmaputra.

rivers.name: Dhansiri
rivers.note: A southern tributary draining the Nagaland–Assam region.

rivers.name: Kopili
rivers.note: A southern tributary of the Brahmaputra system.
rivers.geometryCoverage: Mapped river segments; not a complete source-to-mouth course

rivers.name: Tawa
rivers.note: An important left-bank tributary of the Narmada.

rivers.name: Hiran
rivers.note: A right-bank tributary of the Narmada.

rivers.name: Banjar
rivers.note: A left-bank tributary of the upper Narmada.

rivers.name: Burhner
rivers.note: A left-bank tributary of the upper Narmada.

rivers.name: Barna
rivers.note: A right-bank tributary of the Narmada.

rivers.name: Orsang
rivers.note: A right-bank tributary meeting the Narmada near Chandod.

rivers.name: Pranhita
rivers.note: Carries the Wardha–Wainganga drainage into the Godavari.

rivers.name: Manjira
rivers.note: A right-bank Godavari tributary.

rivers.name: Purna
rivers.note: A left-bank Godavari tributary; distinct from the Tapi-basin Purna.

rivers.name: Pravara
rivers.note: A right-bank tributary of the upper Godavari.

rivers.name: Penganga
rivers.note: Joins the Wardha within the Pranhita–Godavari system.

rivers.name: Wardha
rivers.note: Joins the Wainganga to form the Pranhita.

rivers.name: Wainganga
rivers.note: Drains into the Pranhita–Godavari system.

rivers.name: Indravati
rivers.note: A major left-bank Godavari tributary flowing through the Bastar region.

rivers.name: Sabari
rivers.note: A left-bank tributary of the lower Godavari.

worldLand.name: Indian Ocean Territories
worldLand.capital: Flying Fish Cove · West Island (territorial centres)

states.name: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

places.name: Kangchenjunga
places.note: Major eastern Himalayan summit on the Sikkim–Nepal border.

places.name: K2
places.note: Second-highest mountain on Earth; located in the Karakoram. Geographic context includes areas beyond current Indian administration.

places.name: Western Ghats
places.note: Long western escarpment of the peninsula. This marker is a representative location, not the full range.

places.name: Karakoram
places.note: High mountain system containing K2; distinguish the range from Karakoram Pass.

places.name: Nanga Parbat
places.note: High Himalayan peak near the western end of the Himalayan arc, beyond current Indian administration.

places.name: Eastern Ghats
places.note: Discontinuous hill ranges cut by east-flowing rivers. Marker represents a location within the range.

places.name: Nanda Devi
places.note: Garhwal Himalayan summit associated with the Nanda Devi sanctuary.

places.name: Kamet
places.note: High Garhwal Himalayan peak near the Tibetan Plateau.

places.name: Satpura Range
places.note: Range south of the Narmada valley; Dhupgarh is a prominent high point.

places.name: Vindhya Range
places.note: Central Indian uplands north of the Narmada valley.

places.name: Aravalli Range
places.note: Ancient range running from the Delhi region towards Gujarat; Guru Shikhar is its highest point.

places.name: Rohtang Pass
places.note: Pass connecting the Kullu valley with Lahaul.

places.name: Jelep La
places.note: Pass close to Nathu La, leading towards the Chumbi Valley.

places.name: Nathu La
places.note: Pass east of Gangtok, associated with the historic trade route to Tibet.

places.name: Sivalik Hills
places.note: Outer Himalayan foothill belt extending across northern India and neighbouring countries.

places.name: Dhauladhar
places.note: Himalayan range rising above the Kangra valley.

places.name: Anamudi
places.note: Highest peak in peninsular India, in the Western Ghats.

places.name: Doddabetta
places.note: Prominent Nilgiri summit near Udhagamandalam.

places.name: Patkai
places.note: Part of the northeastern hill system along the India–Myanmar region.

places.name: Cardamom Hills
places.note: Southern Western Ghats hill region.

places.name: Garo Hills
places.note: Western part of the Meghalaya hill system.

places.name: Khasi Hills
places.note: Part of the Meghalaya Plateau, east of the Garo Hills.

places.name: Palakkad Gap
places.note: Broad gap in the Western Ghats connecting the Palakkad and Coimbatore regions.

places.name: Banihal Pass
places.note: Pass across the Pir Panjal south of the Kashmir valley.

places.name: Naga Hills
places.note: Northeastern hill system associated with Saramati.

places.name: Pangsau Pass
places.note: Pass on the historic Stillwell Road near Nampong.

places.name: Pir Panjal Range
places.note: Himalayan range associated with Banihal and Pir Panjal passes.

places.name: Guru Shikhar
places.note: Highest point in the Aravalli Range, near Mount Abu.

places.name: Karakoram Pass
places.note: High pass on the historic caravan route between Ladakh and Central Asia.

places.name: Zanskar Range
places.note: High mountain range between the Kashmir-Himachal region and the Tibetan Plateau.

places.name: Bara-lacha la
places.note: High pass in the Lahaul region on the Manali–Leh corridor.

places.name: Shipki La
places.note: Pass in the Kinnaur region near the Sutlej corridor.

places.name: Lipulekh Pass
places.note: High pass associated with the Kailash–Mansarovar route.

places.name: Sandakphu
places.note: High point of the Singalila ridge near the West Bengal–Nepal border.

places.name: Nilgiri Mountains
places.note: Southern hill junction of the Western and Eastern Ghats; Doddabetta is a key peak.

places.name: Trisul
places.note: Three-peaked Himalayan group southwest of Nanda Devi.

places.name: Kedarnath Peak
places.note: Garhwal Himalayan peak; this marker represents the mountain, not Kedarnath town or temple.

places.name: Thal Ghat
places.note: Western Ghats pass corridor near Kasara, connecting the Konkan with the plateau.

places.name: Mana Pass
places.note: High pass north of Badrinath in the Garhwal Himalaya.

places.name: Dhupgarh
places.note: Prominent summit of the Satpura hills near Pachmarhi.

places.name: Sela Pass
places.note: High pass on the route between West Kameng and Tawang.

places.name: Zoji La
places.note: Pass linking the Kashmir valley with the Dras–Kargil region.

places.name: Mount Saramati
places.note: Major summit of the Naga Hills on the India–Myanmar border.
